title: Egress multipath PMTU & TLS reset diary
content:
Context:
- Private deployment (on-prem connector) peered to customer VPC via TGW/Transit Gateway + static peering. Intermittent TLS handshakes failing when client app talks to hosted control-plane endpoints over the peering path. Issue only affects ~10% of connections and correlates with larger payloads / long TLS records (SNI present).

Symptoms seen:
- App logs: "TLS handshake failed: EOF" or "remote error: tls: bad record MAC" (Go net/http)
- At times openssl s_client shows: 
    $ openssl s_client -connect 10.50.200.12:443 -servername api.redwood.local
    CONNECTED(00000003)
    140735244551872:error:1425F102:SSL routines:ssl_choose_client_version:unsupported protocol:../ssl/statem/statem_clnt.c:1940
- tcpdump shows SYN/SYN-ACK then client sends large segment with MSS > 1400 and subsequent retransmits; Peer sends RST after TLS ClientHello (not consistently).
- mtr/traceroute occasionally show asymmetric next-hop during fail window (two possible egress links).

Commands and captures tried (raw excerpts):
- tcpdump (capture at host):
    21:01:05.123456 IP 10.10.1.5.43210 > 10.50.200.12.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
    21:01:05.123789 IP 10.50.200.12.443 > 10.10.1.5.43210: Flags [S.], seq 54321, ack 12346, win 28960, options [mss 1460], length 0
    21:01:05.124002 IP 10.10.1.5.43210 > 10.50.200.12.443: Flags [P.], seq 12346:12746, ack 54322, win 65535, length 400  # ClientHello (fragment?)
    21:01:05.124100 IP 10.50.200.12.443 > 10.10.1.5.43210: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0, length 0

- ss -tnp on host while reproducing:
    ESTAB  0  0  10.10.1.5:43210  10.50.200.12:443  users:("go")
    TIME_WAIT entries spike after failures

- ip route show / ip rule show:
    default via 10.10.1.1 dev eth0 proto static
    10.50.200.0/24 via 10.10.2.1 dev eth1

- iptables conntrack snapshot: many RELATED,ESTABLISHED entries but also "INVALID" hits for failing flows

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) PMTU / fragmentation blackhole: large ClientHello fragments (SNI + ALPN + cert compression) exceed path MTU on one of the multipath legs causing downstream device to drop fragments. TCP retransmit patterns + RST from peer suggest remote stack rejecting reassembly.
2) Asymmetric routing + stateful firewall: return traffic routed via different egress that doesn't have conntrack entries leading to RSTs. Correlates with traceroute showing two egresses.
3) Middlebox (NAT/IPS) on peering path clamps MSS or injects RST when seeing TLS ClientHello > X bytes (pattern-based).
4) TCP offload/segmentation issue on local NIC (GSO/TSO) causing incorrect on-wire segment sizes toward older peering equipment.

Mitigations & tests performed and results:
- Forced MTU clamp on local egress (ip link set dev eth1 mtu 1400): reduced failure rate from ~10% to ~2% during 4h test window. Suggests PMTU contributes.
- Disabled GSO/TSO (ethtool -K eth1 gso off tso off): no change in visible failure pattern (still occasional drops).
- Added iptables mangle TCPMSS clamp (iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu): immediate improvement; handshake success rose to ~99% in short run.
- Reproduced openssl s_client with -ign_eof to force larger fragments; without MSS clamp, peer sometimes RSTs. With clamp, OK.
- Verified conntrack settings: net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established = 432000 (default), nf_conntrack_max plenty. No exhaustion.

Next actions planned / TODOs:
- Confirm whether AWS Transit Gateway or customer edge appliance is dropping fragments. Ask customer to check metal edge logs around timestamps (ticket created).
- Add persistent MSS clamp on peering host as stopgap. Document with clear rollback steps.
- Run controlled test matrix: varying MTU (1500/1460/1400/1300), toggling GSO/TSO, with and without TCPMSS clamp, capture pcap from both ends.
- Engage infra networking to look at ECMP hashing — set pinning to prefer single path for testing window.
- If middlebox suspected, collect TLS ClientHello raw hex (pcap) to show size pattern and send to customer SOC for signature match.

Notes to self / gotchas:
- Don’t assume 'bad record MAC' always equals crypto bug; often a truncated/shifted record due to MTU/fragment drop results in garbage MACs post-decryption.
- Be careful when flipping MSS clamps across NATing boxes — double-clamping can cause suboptimal MSS. Document where clamp is applied (host vs router).
- When filetting pcap for redaction, keep timestamps and packet lengths; security will want both.

Linked debugging artifacts (local):
- /var/log/peering/peering-2026-02-18.pcap (captured at host eth1)
- /home/maya/tmp/openssl-clienthello-hex.txt

References / links:
- Jira: NET-1347 (customer peering intermittent TLS resets)
- Confluence: confluence.redwood.local/display/NET/Peering+MSS+Clamp+Playbook

Collaborators: Maya Chen, Sanjay Patel, Emeka Okoye (customer SRE), Luca Moretti (infra-net)
